title: Days Allowed to Cure — Calculation Note for Hardship and Protective Holds
content:
For Hardship and Protective Holds, a cure notice on an undecided hold request states the days allowed to cure. This note defines that figure.

## Definition

The notice asks for the kind of documentation carried by the latest submission received on the request, and states the days allowed to cure: the number of calendar days, counted from the day the notice is sent, within which the completed documentation must arrive. The days allowed to cure run from the day the notice is sent to the due date of the original documentation request for that same kind of documentation. The days allowed to cure are a whole number of calendar days and are not rounded.

## The quantities and where they are read

| Quantity | Read from |
|---|---|
| The kind of documentation | The latest documentation submission received on the request, in the hold's history |
| The original due date | The due date of the original documentation request for that same kind, in the hold's history |
| The day the notice is sent | The day the notice goes out |
| Days allowed to cure | The calendar days from the day the notice is sent to the original due date |

The cure due date is then the day the notice is sent plus the days allowed to cure.

## Worked example (hypothetical)

A request's latest submission, received on 9 May, carries household income records. The original documentation request for household income records on that request has a due date of 20 May. The notice is sent on 12 May.

- Calendar days from 12 May to 20 May: 8.
- Days allowed to cure: 8, a whole number with no rounding.
- Cure due date: 12 May plus 8 days, that is 20 May.

## Second example (hypothetical)

The latest submission carries a physician's medical or disability certification; the original documentation request for that kind is due on 3 June; the notice goes out on 25 May. From 25 May to 3 June is 9 calendar days, so the days allowed to cure are 9 and the cure due date is 3 June.
